overall_assessment: Track 22 establishes rigorous methodological governance for living systematic reviews in accordance with PRISMA-LSR (2024) and Cochrane living review guidance. The reporting pack prisma-lsr-2024 is strictly bounded to reporting considerations (cadence and version lineage) without masquerading as conduct rules. The protocol amendment schema mandates explicit rationales, before/after diffs, retrospective impact assessments, and designated decision-makers. Crucially, the living update contract enforces a mandatory human release gate whenever record changes occur, forbidding automated inclusion into screening pipelines.

findings.description: PRISMA-LSR pack items currently address update frequency and version lineage; future extensions should define crosswalks for ongoing trial registry status transitions (e.g. recruiting to completed).
findings.recommendation: Expand standard pack crosswalks when Track 23 (Trial registries and ongoing studies) contracts are integrated.

findings.description: Protocol amendments support retrospective impact narrative, but structured impact metrics (e.g. number of previously screened records requiring reassessment) are currently captured as text.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding optional structured record re-screening count tallies in amendment contracts.

findings.description: LivingUpdateRun validation strictly fails closed if changes exist and requires_human_release is false, providing guaranteed human-in-the-loop protection against unverified screening drift.
findings.recommendation: Preserve this invariant across all downstream execution harnesses and MCP endpoints.

calibration_notes: Methodologists will unanimously commend the separation of reporting requirements from conduct rules and the strict human release mandate preventing silent review drift.
